title: Presentability of coherent space-valued presheaves
statement:
Fix nested universes as in [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and let $D$ be a small ordinary category. Let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of small spaces, modeled by Kan complexes with their full homotopy coherent mapping spaces, and let $N(D)$ be the ordinary nerve. The infinity category of space-valued presheaves
$$\mathcal P(N(D))=\operatorname{Fun}(N(D)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$$
is presentable: it has all small colimits and, for some regular cardinal $\kappa$ in the smaller universe, is generated under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose mapping-space functors preserve those colimits. This is a statement about coherent functors into spaces, including their natural transformations and higher homotopies.

source.place: Remark 5.5.3.7; alternatively Example 5.5.1.8 and Proposition 5.5.3.6 (printed pp. 461, 467-468). Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $C=N(D)$ and $B=C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Their simplices are finite strings of arrows of the small category $D$, so $C$ and $B$ are small. The discrete simplicial category on $D$ is locally Kan; [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies its coherent nerve with $N(D)$ and makes it a quasicategory. Use the coherent functor category of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. By [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback], $\mathcal S$ is presentable and has all small colimits. To construct a colimit of an arbitrary small diagram $H:J\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S)$, regard it as $B\times J\to\mathcal S$. Let $P\subseteq B$ be the discrete simplicial subset of all its vertices, and choose a colimiting cocone on $H(b,-)$ for each vertex $b$. These choices give the prescribed map on $(B\times J)\amalg_{P\times J}(P\times J^{\triangleright})$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-parameter-cone-extension]: $P$ contains every vertex and every required initial-vertex cocone is colimiting, so it supplies an extension $B\times J^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal S$. Thus the pointwise cocones do assemble coherently. The objectwise characterization in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] now says that this is a colimit cocone in $\mathcal P(C)$. It also says that evaluation at any $c$ preserves it. This works for every small simplicial $J$, including $J=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.5.10, Corollaries 5.1.2.2-5.1.2.4, and Example 5.5.1.8. Read online; the assembly and cardinal bookkeeping here are written by the worker.

proof.text: We record the needed universe bound without replacing mapping spaces by sets of components. Use the model of $\mathcal S$ as the coherent nerve of small Kan complexes with their simplicial mapping complexes. For any small family $T$ of presheaves, the collection of Kan complexes $F(c)$, for $F\in T$ and $c\in C_0$, is small. The full simplicial category on this collection has small mapping complexes: their $n$-simplices are maps $A\times\Delta^n\to B$ between small simplicial sets. Its coherent nerve $\mathcal S_T$ is small, since the formula for $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] uses finitely many objects and small mapping data in each degree; it is a quasicategory by that node. It is the full subcategory of the chosen model of $\mathcal S$ on these Kan complexes. Every presheaf in $T$ factors through $\mathcal S_T$, and $\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_T)$ is a small full simplicial subcategory of $\mathcal P(C)$: its simplices are maps between small simplicial sets, and fullness follows degreewise from the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The full subcategory on the objects of $T$ is therefore small in this model. Taking $T=\{F,G\}$ proves that every mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(F,G)$ is small. In particular $\mathcal P(C)$ is locally small. We will also use the same construction for the family of generators below.

source.place: Coherent-nerve construction in section 1.1.5 and Proposition 1.1.5.10; explicit universe bookkeeping for full subcategories of presheaves. Read online; the assembly and cardinal bookkeeping here are written by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the one-member family with value $\mathbb N$. It gives an infinite regular $\kappa$ in the smaller universe with $\aleph_0<\kappa$. For each vertex $c$ of $C$, [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(h_c,-)$ naturally with evaluation at $c$. Step 1 and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] show that this evaluation preserves every small colimit. Thus each $h_c$ is $\kappa$-compact in precisely the mapping-space sense of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. No claim is made that every presheaf is already a filtered colimit of individual representables.

source.place: Lemmas 5.1.5.2-5.1.5.3 and Corollary 5.1.2.3; compactness definition in section 5.3.4. Read online; the assembly and cardinal bookkeeping here are written by the worker.

proof.text: Let $A$ be a set of representative pairs $(K,p)$ with $K$ a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and $p:K\to C$ a simplicial map. This can be chosen small: since $\kappa$ is uncountable, the degeneracies of fewer than $\kappa$ nondegenerate simplices still form fewer than $\kappa$ simplices. Relabel them by a subset of the fixed set $\kappa$; the degree sets, simplicial operators and maps to the fixed small set of simplices of $C$ then range over subsets and functions on fixed small sets. Their collection is small in the smaller universe, even though it need not have size less than $\kappa$. For every representative choose a colimiting cocone on $h\circ p$, using step 1, and let $\mathcal G$ be the small family of its apices. These are choices of universal objects, determined up to equivalence by the displayed diagrams. All vertex values $h_{p(v)}$ are $\kappa$-compact by step 3, and $\mathcal P(C)$ is locally small and has all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by steps 1-2. Therefore [lem-coef-compact-small-colimits] makes every object of $\mathcal G$ $\kappa$-compact. Include the representative $K=\varnothing$, so the initial presheaf is among these apices. The small-full-subcategory construction of step 2, applied to $\mathcal G$, gives a small full subcategory $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P(C)$ on these chosen objects.

source.place: Bounded-diagram family in the proof of Proposition 5.3.5.12; Corollary 5.3.4.15. Relabeling and universe bookkeeping are written out here. Read online; the assembly and cardinal bookkeeping here are written by the worker.

proof.text: Fix any presheaf $F$. By [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] it has a colimiting coherent cocone $h\circ p_F\to F$ on a small simplicial set $E_F$. Apply [lem-coef-colimit-subdiagram-approximation] to this diagram in $\mathcal P(C)$, which has all small colimits by step 1, with the uncountable regular cardinal of step 3. For each $\kappa$-small simplicial subset $L\subseteq E_F$, relabel $(L,p_F|_L)$ by its representative in $A$ and transport the already chosen colimiting cocone from step 4 along that isomorphism. Thus its apex $q_L$ is literally one of the chosen objects of $\mathcal G$. The prescribed-cocone clause of the approximation node assembles these very apices into a coherent diagram $Q:N(I_\kappa(E_F))\to\mathcal P(C)$ and a colimiting cocone $Q\to F$. Every vertex of $Q$ belongs to $\mathcal A$, so, by the definition of a full subcategory in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the entire simplicial map $Q$ factors through $\mathcal A$. Its index is small and $\kappa$-filtered by the approximation node. Consequently every $F$ is a small $\kappa$-filtered colimit of objects of the same small full subcategory $\mathcal A$. We require only universe-smallness of this index, not that it has fewer than $\kappa$ elements.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3; Proposition 4.2.3.4, Remark 4.2.3.9, Corollary 4.2.3.10, and the directed-union construction in the proof of Corollary 4.2.3.11. Read online; the assembly and cardinal bookkeeping here are written by the worker.

proof.text: Steps 1-2 give local smallness and all small colimits of $\mathcal P(C)$. Steps 3-5 give a regular cardinal $\kappa$ in the smaller universe and a small full subcategory $\mathcal A$ of $\kappa$-compact objects generating every presheaf under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits. These are exactly the clauses of $\kappa$-accessibility in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Together with all small simplicial colimits, that definition gives presentability. With $C=N(D)$ this is the stated assertion. If $D$ is empty, the bounded family still includes the empty colimit, the presheaf category is terminal, and the same construction applies; no nonemptiness hypothesis has been added.

source.place: Remark 5.5.3.7, with the accessibility argument expanded as in Proposition 5.3.5.12. Read online; the assembly and cardinal bookkeeping here are written by the worker.

split_report.summary: Kept the item statement unchanged. Constructed all coherent colimits from objectwise cocones using the existing parameter-cone extension theorem, rather than assuming coherent assembly from a pointwise characterization. Proved local smallness and smallness of the full generator family in the concrete Kan/coherent-nerve model. Chose an uncountable regular bound, proved representables compact by evaluation, formed a bounded small family of compact colimits of representables, and reconstructed arbitrary presheaves as filtered colimits of that family. Three genuinely smaller foundational statements are unsplit; no ordinary Mathlib analogue is treated as an infinity-categorical match.
